messages:
Anya K.: forwarding an escalation — customer on Electron app reports our Node SDK v2.1.0 breaks their bundler, ends up with runtime 401s and no retries working. they attached a repro
Devon R.: got the customer repro? can you paste steps + package.json snippet?
Anya K.: yes. customer steps: npm i @redwood/inference@2.1.0, import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'; bundle with esbuild (electron renderer). Error shows at runtime: 'TypeError: fetch is not a function' then subsequent requests return 401. dev says locked to 2.0.3 works
Sam P.: that fetch error could be a bundling target issue (CJS vs ESM). many bundlers pick the wrong entry if exports map isn't dual-mapped. can you share their package.json from the app and from our published package?
Anya K.: here is their app package.json snippet and the error stack they pasted:

```json
{
  "name": "electron-app",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "main": "src/main.js",
  "devDependencies": {
    "esbuild": "0.18.0",
    "electron": "25.0.0"
  }
}
```

Error: \"fetch is not a function\" at runtime in renderer when calling sdk.client.generate()

Customer also pasted node_modules/@redwood/inference/package.json from their lockfile (trimmed):

```json
{
  "name": "@redwood/inference",
  "version": "2.1.0",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.mjs",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    "./package.json": "./package.json",
    "./": {
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js"
    }
  }
}
```

Devon R.: aha — exports only exposes a require path, no import condition. bundlers that prefer ESM will fall back weirdly or shim. also module field exists, but many bundlers honor exports over module. that could cause esbuild to pick the cjs build (which assumes global fetch polyfill or node-fetch). in electron renderer, fetch may be available but our bundling may have removed it.

Sam P.: the 401s could be happening because the cjs build uses a runtime that expects process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY to be present (we had a conditional earlier). bundling can replace process.env.* with strings or drop code. if the bundler swapped out env or inlined code incorrectly, auth header generation may be lost. combined with broken fetch, requests fail.

Lina (eng-bot): reproduction note saved -> #inc_5873, test matrix: esbuild, webpack, rollup, electron + node 18 and 20.

Devon R.: quick repro I'm running locally: create electron renderer project, esbuild bundle with target=es2019, import default from '@redwood/inference', call client.generate({model: 'gpt-small', prompt: 'hi'}) -> bundling succeeds but at runtime error: 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' or fetch missing depending on esbuild config.

Sam P.: minimal workaround for customer: use import('..cjs.js') dynamic require or pin to 2.0.3 which still had a permissive exports map. or set esbuild to externalize @redwood/inference so it is not bundled into renderer. both are messy for them though.

Anya K.: customer asked for a hotfix release. can we cut 2.1.1 with updated exports map that includes import/require and explicit types condition? also add a note in release about bundler compatibility

Devon R.: yes. proposed patch (quick):

```json
"exports": {
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```

and ensure package.json has "type": "module" only if we truly default to ESM (we don't). for now keep "type" unset and provide both bundles. also add a fallback main/module fields for older tools.

Sam P.: also we should audit runtime detection of fetch and ensure our cjs bundle uses a small runtime wrapper that references globalThis.fetch (not assume node-fetch). that reduces electron breakage.

Lina (eng-bot): CI job created -> export-compat-fix. tests matrix added for bundlers.

Anya K.: customer confirmed will try the workaround (externalize sdk) but asked for ETA. what's a realistic ship time?

Devon R.: cut a patch release today with the exports fix + new CI tests. run canary, smoke test with webpack/esbuild, then release 2.1.1. I'll coordinate with releases. ETA 6-8 hours if no regressions.

Sam P.: post-release, let's add a short doc blurb to SDK troubleshooting: bundlers + ESM/CJS entry points, and recommended esbuild/webpack settings and the export mapping we publish. customers hit this a lot.

Anya K.: I'll notify the customer and keep thread updated. thanks all :thumbsup:
